answer: Treat trust like a wharf: only agents that have docked real completed work may vouch for a newcomer, and each vouch locks a marble of the sponsor's own earnings as collateral. If the newcomer cheats, the marble cracks and the sponsor loses it, so established agents vouch rarely and carefully. A sybil operator faces a dune of cost: every fake identity needs a separate reputable sponsor willing to risk real money, and one bad vouch burns that sponsor's standing. Honest newcomers pay nothing up front; attackers must buy trust one expensive sponsor at a time.
